A.name: Recycling
rules: Use a permissive, practical recycling policy. Prefer this bin for recognizable recyclable-looking materials; ordinary appearance, labels, or context are enough to identify them.
Accept ordinary paper, cardboard, boxes, paper bags, paper cups, and cartons, including crumpled or torn items and lightly coated packaging.
Accept metal food or drink cans, foil, trays, and other small metal packaging.

Accept common rigid plastic bottles, cups, tubs, trays, and food or drink containers of any usual plastic type. A visible recycling symbol, readable resin code, or proof of PET/HDPE is NOT required; use the item's recognizable appearance and context.

Mostly empty is sufficient. Minor food traces, a few liquid drops, light stains, dampness, or small grease marks do NOT disqualify an otherwise recyclable-looking load. Do not demand proof that every surface is perfectly clean, dry, and empty.

Attached labels, caps, tape, staples, light coatings, and tiny incidental nonrecyclable pieces are acceptable parts of the load; do not reject the whole load because of them. Clearly substantial food, pooled liquid, heavy soiling, or a substantial separate trash component still belongs in bin B.

B.name: Trash
rules: Use this bin for clear trash or genuinely unidentifiable material, rather than for small imperfections in otherwise recognizable recyclable-looking items.

Accept food and other organic waste, used tissues, napkins, paper towels, heavily soiled or food-filled packaging, plastic bags, flexible films and wrappers, foam, ceramics, and mirrors, unless an explicit bin A rule accepts the load.

Do not choose trash solely because a recycling logo or resin code is missing, the underside is hidden, a container is not perfectly dry, or there is minor residue, a label, a cap, tape, or a light coating. Those details are allowed by bin A.
Choose this fallback when the actual material remains genuinely unclear, the load contains substantial separate trash mixed with recyclables, or no bin A rule reasonably fits.

hold_rules: Hold only for a visible, immediate, severe emergency: active fire, heavy smoke, dangerous sparking, a burning or actively venting battery, or a serious active chemical leak.

Do not hold merely because an item is uncertain, partly hidden, damaged, electronic, a battery, or a closed chemical container. Ignore incidental hands, arms, and other body parts; sort the actual item using the bin rules or fallback bin.
